headline: N-able takes platform offline after zero-day disclosure, then issues hotfixes
summary: N-able took its hosted N-central environments offline and urged self-hosted customers to shut down their own servers after a researcher publicly disclosed dozens of zero-day vulnerabilities that could let attackers take over systems. N-able later released security hotfixes addressing the bugs.

claims.statement: N-able took its remote-access/cloud platform offline and urged self-hosted customers to shut down their servers after a researcher disclosed dozens of zero-day vulnerabilities.

sources.quote: N-able takes cloud platform offline after 30+ "zero-days" published
N-able takes its remote access service offline after researcher publishes dozens of zero-day bugs
The remote access giant also urged its self-hosted customers to take down their own servers amid a "critical security incident," fearing the possibility of cyberattacks.

claims.statement: N-able released security hotfixes addressing the disclosed zero-day vulnerabilities.

sources.quote: N-able releases security hotfixes for zero-day vulnerabilities

N-able released hotfixes to address zero-day bugs affecting its N-central remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform, which were publicly disclosed over the weekend and forced it to take vulnerable hosted environments offline.
